The '''Miguel de Cervantes Prize''' ({{langx|es|Premio de Literatura en Lengua Castellana Miguel de Cervantes}}) is awarded annually to honour the lifetime achievement of an outstanding writer in the [[Spanish language]]. The ''[[Encyclopædia Britannica]]'' calls it the "most prestigious and remunerative award given for Spanish-language literature".<ref name=brit/>

==History==
The prize was established in 1975 by the [[Ministry of Culture of Spain]] and first awarded the following year.<ref name=brit>{{cite web|url=http://www.britannica.com/EBchecked/topic/103671/Cervantes-Prize |title=Cervantes Prize | award |website=Britannica.com |date=2014-11-25 |access-date=2017-02-27}}</ref> The winner receives a monetary award of 125,000 [[euro]]s, which makes it one of the [[List of the world's richest literary prizes|richest literary prizes in the world]].<ref name=wolfe>{{cite web |url=https://artsbeat.blogs.nytimes.com/2015/11/12/fernando-del-paso-wins-miguel-de-cervantes-prize/ |title=Fernando del Paso Wins Miguel de Cervantes Prize |work=New York Times |author=Jonathan Wolfe |date=November 12, 2015 |access-date=November 17, 2017}}</ref> The prize rewards authors from any [[Hispanophone|Spanish-speaking]] nation and recognizes the recipient's overall body of work.<ref name=brit/> Of the forty-seven prizes awarded in the history of the Cervantes Prize, only six have ever been awarded to women. In 1988, the Spanish writer [[María Zambrano]] (1904–1991) was the first female writer to be honored. The award is named after [[Miguel de Cervantes]], author of ''[[Don Quixote]]''.<ref name=wolfe/> The candidates are proposed by the [[Association of Spanish Language Academies]] (i.e., the [[Royal Spanish Academy]]).<ref>{{cite web |date=2014 |title=Miguel de Cervantes |url=https://www.donquijote.org/es/lengua-espanola/escritores-espanoles/miguel-de-cervantes/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230604032251/https://www.donquijote.org/es/lengua-espanola/escritores-espanoles/miguel-de-cervantes/ |archive-date=4 June 2023 |access-date=4 June 2023 |work=donquijote.org}}</ref>

As of the presentation of the 2024 award to [[Álvaro Pombo]], the recipients have been recognized for their writing of novels, poetry, short stories, essays, translations, philosophy or dramas{{snd}}or for combinations thereof. With two winners in 1979, there have been 50 recipients of the Miguel de Cervantes Prize.

===The Cervantes Prize and the Nobel Prize in Literature===
Three of the 50 winners of the Miguel de Cervantes Prize have also won the [[Nobel Prize in Literature]]. [[Octavio Paz]] (Cervantes 1981, Nobel 1990) and [[Mario Vargas Llosa]] (Cervantes 1994, Nobel 2010), were awarded the Nobel Prize in subsequent years, while [[Camilo José Cela]] received the Nobel Prize in 1989 and was awarded the Cervantes Prize in 1995.
